title: Mulligatawny Soup
servings: Serves: 6 as a starter or 4 as a main course

ingredients.title: For the Soup Base
items: Coconut milk or cream – ½ cup
Lemon or lime juice – from 1 lemon or lime
Fresh coriander leaves – chopped, for garnish

instruction.title: Sauté the Aromatics
steps: Heat the ghee or oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add mustard seeds and cumin seeds and allow them to splutter.
Add the chopped onion and sauté for 8–10 minutes until soft and golden brown.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and green chilies.
Cook for 2–3 minutes until fragrant.

instruction.title: Toast the Spices
steps: Add turmeric powder, ground coriander, garam masala, cinnamon, and cloves.
Stir well to coat the aromatics.
Cook for 1–2 minutes over medium heat to gently toast the spices and release their aroma.

instruction.title: Add the Vegetables & Lentils
steps: Add diced carrot, diced apple, and rinsed red lentils.
Stir well to combine with the spiced onion mixture.

instruction.title: Simmer the Soup
steps: Pour in the chicken or vegetable stock.
Bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes.
Cook until the lentils and vegetables are completely tender.

instruction.title: Blend the Soup
steps: Use an immersion blender to puree the soup to your preferred consistency.
Alternatively, carefully blend in batches using a regular blender.
Keep the soup completely smooth or leave it slightly chunky according to preference.

instruction.title: Finish the Soup
steps: Stir in the coconut milk or cream.
Simmer gently for another 5 minutes to heat through.
Season with salt and fresh lemon or lime juice.
Taste and adjust the seasoning as needed.
If using cooked chicken or tofu, add it and warm through before serving.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Ladle the hot soup into serving bowls.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve with a lemon or lime wedge on the side.
Serve with warm naan or crusty bread if desired.

chefTips: Apple: Green apple adds subtle sweetness and balances the spices, so it is worth including.
Spices: Gently toast the spices with the aromatics to release deeper flavor without burning them.
Texture: Blend completely smooth for a refined soup or leave slightly chunky for a more rustic texture.
Extra depth: Add about 1 tsp tamarind paste or mango chutney for an additional sweet-tangy layer.
Protein: Cooked chicken works well for a non-vegetarian version, while cubed tofu makes a suitable vegetarian option.
Serving: Warm naan or crusty bread pairs especially well with the rich, aromatic soup.
